source.title: Safety Alignment Can Be Not Superficial With Explicit Safety Signals

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-completion attack success rates under prefilling and decoding attacks, using a different safety mechanism and evaluation setup from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper tests prefilling and decoding attacks on its safety-enhanced model and measures output entropy and sharpness under different prompt conditions. It does not test harmful-example or benign-data fine-tuning as a cause of refusal loss, per-position aligned-versus-base KL, or safety localization in weights. Results cited from other work in Table 2 are not recorded. Table 1 and Table 3 contain attack results whose flattened layout does not support secure assignment of all numbers to conditions and models; those results are noted in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study's own baselines show prefilling and decoding attacks overriding refusal in conventionally aligned 7B models (V4). Its explicit-safety-signal method re-checks safety throughout generation, and its prefill, decoding and nested-attack results show whether such a fix holds up (V7). Both use a different method and setup from the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors trace superficial alignment to implicit safety signals being diluted by competing objectives. They conclude that an explicit [CLS] safety classification task, combined with strategic attention and decoding that re-assess safety during generation, sharply reduces jailbreak, prefill and decoding-attack ASR at under 0.2x overhead.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a binary classification objective and [CLS]-based dynamic attention and decoding; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefill length and wording, decoding parameters, classification threshold, reclassification frequency, attention window sizes, and the model/checkpoint affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama2-7B-Chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 show higher top-100-logit entropy and lower sharpness going from Direct to Prefill to Nested prompts (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial prompt complexity raises next-token uncertainty in aligned models. This is not an aligned-versus-base per-position KL measure.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The authors state that compute limits prevented validation on models larger than 10B and restricted evaluations of optimization-based attacks. The pretraining stage uses weak safety labels that may be noisy and did not yield substantial gains. The paper reports ASR as its safety metric and notes false positives in Llama3-Guard. Several attack-result tables are flattened in the provided text, making some model-to-value assignments uncertain.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports additional prefill, GCG, AutoDAN-T, DeepInception, PAP, Alert-Adversarial, and decoding results, but the flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of every value to a model and condition. Table 3's cross-family table has a similarly ambiguous number of entries. Table 2's starred Llama2-7B-Chat and Llama2-7B-Chat-Aug results are identified as excerpted from the original paper and were not recorded as this study's own results.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning of safety-trained models, including of the CLS model.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models; the entropy and sharpness probe is a different construct.

No suffix or GCG results on undefended baselines that can be securely assigned (the Table 1 layout is ambiguous for some columns). The Llama2-7B-Chat prefill/decoding values in Table 2 are excerpted from Qi et al.
Argues that implicit safety signals are diluted by competing objectives, but runs no test of whether data or objective causes first-token shallowness.
No per-position measure of safety depth for the CLS model. No fine-tuning-attack robustness of the fixed model. GCG not compared against Qi et al.'s augmented model.

missing.what: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 ASR: direct 42.31% vs prefill 92.12% (AdvBench), 49.7% vs 90.91% (HEx-PHI); Mistral-CLS prefill 0.4%/2.12%, DeepInception 10%
Llama2-7B-CLS jailbreak results, including DeepInception 2.0% (the only case worse than a baseline), GCG 0%, and AutoDAN 0.77%
missing.locator: Table 1, CLS column (third value list) and caption text

missing.what: Sensitivity of DeepInception ASR to classification threshold (6–66%), r2 (6–14%) and τ (2–14%)
CLS model without the [CLS] token reverts to SFT-level direct ASR (1.15%, 3.03%)
Ablation: removing strategic attention or strategic decoding raises ASR

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the CLS-model rows to V4 and called the low ASR 'challenges'. That is wrong: low ASR on a defended model shows the defense works, not that prefilling fails on ordinary alignment. Those rows are relinked to V7. The CLS method is a train-plus-inference re-check rather than data augmentation; treat it as a V7-type fix, but its depth is not measured per position. In Table 1 the Llama2-7B-Chat and CLS columns are interleaved in the flattened text. Table 3's Llama2-7B-Chat values match Table 1's SFT-DPO column, so the Llama2-7B-Chat attributions are uncertain and are not used for verdicts. Table 2's Chat and Chat-Aug values are cited from Qi et al. The study uses a different ASR judge from Qi et al. (it counts all harmful scores, not only level 5), so the cross-paper comparison in Table 2 is not like-for-like.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning safety-trained models on a few to a few hundred harmful examples or measure resulting refusal loss.
Does not test whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Measures entropy and sharpness under attack conditions, not per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.

Reports prefilling and decoding-attack results for the CLS-enhanced model. It discusses suffix and other jailbreak attacks, but exact results for those conditions are not extracted because the relevant table layout is ambiguous.
Does not localize safety behaviour to weights, ranks, or a small parameter subset.
Argues that implicit safety signals can be diluted by competing objectives, but does not directly test whether the data or objective used in conventional alignment causes first-token shallowness.
Introduces dynamic safety reassessment and reports attack outcomes, but does not measure whether training spreads safety across response positions or directly measure safety depth.

relationships.reason: Based on the text; no rows. SFT ASR rises from 1.15% (direct) to 92.7% with prefill on AdvBench, and decoding ASR reaches 98%/89%. Mistral rises from 42.31% to 92.12% (AdvBench) and from 49.7% to 90.91% (HEx-PHI).
